verses.1: And Joshua gathered all the officials of Israel together. He called upon the elders of Israel, their leaders, judges, and officers. They stood before the LORD.
verses.2: And Joshua said to all the people, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, has commanded, let your ancestors dwell in their land forever. May Abraham’s father and Noah’s father also dwell there. They will serve other gods instead.”
verses.3: And I will take your father, Abraham, across the river. I will go with him throughout all the land of Canaan. I will spread his descendants over that land, and I will give Isaac to him.
verses.4: And I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau. And I gave Esau Mount Seir, so that he could possess it. Then Jacob and his sons went down from Egypt.
verses.5: And I will send Moses and Aaron to take away the Egyptians, just as I did during their time. After I brought you out from there.
verses.6: And I will bring your ancestors out of Egypt. They will come in that day, and they will pursue those who fled from Egypt after their ancestors. They will do so on chariots and horses, and in wagons across the sea of Suez.
verses.7: They cried out to the LORD, and He put a barrier between you and the Egyptians. The sea covered them, and you saw with your own eyes what I did to the Egyptians. They were trapped on the shore for many days.
verses.8: And I will bring you to the land of the Amorites, who live across the Jordan. They will fight against you, but I will give them over to your hands. Then they will inherit their land, and I will drive them away from before you.
verses.9: And Balak, the king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent Bileam, son of Beor, to curse you.
verses.10: And I did not want to hear from Belial. He blessed you, and he held you in his hands.
verses.11: And they crossed the Jordan and entered Jericho. They fought against the people of Jericho: the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivvites, and the Gebusites. And they dealt with them as they saw fit.
verses.12: And I will send the locusts before you. They will drive them away from you. It was two Amorite kings who did this, not during your reign, nor during your time of weakness.
verses.13: And I will give you land that you will not tread upon, and cities that you did not build. There, grapes and figs will grow, and you will eat them.
verses.14: And now, let them see Jehovah and worship Him in truth and sincerity. Let them put away the gods they worshipped their ancestors before the river and in Egypt. Let them worship Jehovah instead.
verses.15: And if it seems bad to you to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves today whom you will serve. Whether it be the gods your ancestors served, who live across the river, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you now live. I and my house will serve the LORD.
verses.16: And the people said, “Alas! Let us be freed from serving Jehovah and from worshiping other gods instead.”
verses.17: For Jehovah our God is the one who has delivered us and our ancestors from the land of Egypt, from being slaves there. He also made these great miracles before our eyes. He protected us along all the paths we traveled, and among all the nations we passed through.
verses.18: And Jehovah will drive out all those nations from before us. Then we too will serve Jehovah, for He is our God.
verses.19: And Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve Yahweh, for He is a holy God. He will not tolerate your sins and transgressions.”
verses.20: For if you abandon Jehovah and serve other gods, then He will turn against you and do you harm. He will destroy you after all that He has done for you.
verses.21: And the people said to Joshua, “Do not serve Jehovah.”
verses.22: And Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses that you have chosen to serve the LORD alone.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”
verses.23: And now, remove the idols that are among you. Turn your hearts toward Jehovah, the God of Israel.
verses.24: And the people said to Joshua, “Serve Jehovah our God!” And their voices were heard.
verses.25: And Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day. He also established laws and regulations for them in Shechem.
verses.26: And Joshua wrote down these words in the book of God’s laws. He also took a large piece of stone and built a altar there, under the sacred tree of Jehovah.
verses.27: And Joshua said to all the people, “Look! This stone will become a witness against you. It will bear witness to all the words of Jehovah that He spoke to us. It will serve as a witness against you, so that you may not be able to deny what Jehovah has said.”
verses.28: And Joshua sent the people to their respective inheritances.
verses.29: After these events, Jehosua ben Nun died. He was the servant of the LORD, at the age of one hundred and ten years old.
verses.30: And they buried him in the territory of his own land, at Timnath Serah, which is located on Mount Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.31: And Israel obeyed the LORD throughout all the days of Joshua. It also obeyed during all the years of those who grew old after Joshua’s time. They knew all the things that the LORD did for Israel.
verses.32: And the possessions of Joseph, which the sons of Israel took back from Egypt, were buried in Shechem, in the part of the field that Jacob bought from the descendants of Hamor, Abi-Shchem. They became the property of Joseph’s descendants.
verses.33: And Elazar, son of Aaron, died. They buried him in the land of Phinehas, his son’s territory, which was given to him on Mount Ebal.
